components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.

example.hanzi: 他十六岁离家出走，独自在城市里生活了三年。
example.pinyin: tā shíliù suì lí jiā chūzǒu, dúzì zài chéngshì lǐ shēnghuóle sān nián.
example.english: He left home at sixteen and lived alone in the city for three years.
example.fact: Young wolves dispersing from their birth pack have been GPS-tracked traveling over 800 kilometers in search of new territory, one of the longest recorded journeys of any land mammal leaving home. Most dispersers travel alone, and researchers in the northern Rockies have found their survival rate is far lower than for wolves that stay with the pack.

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — 登 relates to climbing or ascending with one's legs
豆 (dòu) gives a sound distantly related to 登's reading dēng, having drifted apart over time
阝 (a hill/place) — 陆 relates to solid ground, as opposed to water
击 (jī) gives a sound distantly related to 陆's reading lù, having drifted apart considerably over time

example.hanzi: 1969年，阿波罗11号成功登陆月球表面。
example.pinyin: yī jiǔ liù jiǔ nián, Ābōluó shíyī hào chénggōng dēnglù yuèqiú biǎomiàn.
example.english: In 1969, Apollo 11 successfully landed on the surface of the moon.
example.fact: The Apollo 11 lunar module touched down with less than 30 seconds of fuel remaining, after Neil Armstrong had to manually steer past a boulder field to a safer landing site. The onboard guidance computer had only about 4KB of RAM, far less processing power than a modern digital watch.

components.note: Flesh/body — the liver is a body organ.
Gives the sound gān, matching the character's reading.
⺼ (flesh) shows 脏 (zàng) relates to the body, as in internal organs.
庄 (zhuāng) gives a sound close to zàng, sharing a similar consonant sound though the vowel and ending differ.

example.hanzi: 肝脏是人体内最大的内脏器官，负责分解毒素。
example.pinyin: gānzàng shì réntǐ nèi zuì dà de nèizàng qìguān, fùzé fēnjiě dúsù.
example.english: The liver is the largest internal organ in the human body, responsible for breaking down toxins.
example.fact: The human liver has remarkable regenerative power — surgeons can remove up to 70 percent of it for a living-donor transplant, and the remaining tissue regrows to nearly its original size within a few months. This is one of the few organs in the body capable of that kind of regrowth.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
扌 (hand) — relates to 据's meaning 'to rely on, according to,' as if grasping evidence in hand.
居 (jū) gave the base sound; the pronunciation later shifted to jù, keeping the same final but a different tone.

example.hanzi: 请保留好这张收据，退货时需要用到。
example.pinyin: qǐng bǎoliú hǎo zhè zhāng shōujù, tuìhuò shí xūyào yòngdào.
example.english: Please keep this receipt, you'll need it if you return the item.
example.fact: Paper receipts printed on thermal paper often contain bisphenol A (BPA), a chemical that can transfer to skin on contact, which is part of why many large retailers have switched to BPA-free paper or digital receipts. Sweden was among the first countries to require that all point-of-sale receipts be offered digitally by law.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 含 originally meant to hold something in the mouth.
今 (jīn) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading hán has diverged.
⺷ (sheep, related to 羊) — 义 relates to what is right or moral, linked to the idea of sacrificial sheep used in rituals of righteousness.
乂 (yì) gives the sound — 义 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这首诗的含义比表面看起来复杂得多。
example.pinyin: zhè shǒu shī de hányì bǐ biǎomiàn kàn qǐlái fùzá de duō.
example.english: The meaning of this poem is much more complex than it appears on the surface.
example.fact: The Rosetta Stone carries the same decree in three scripts — hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Greek — and it was the parallel Greek text that finally let scholars unlock the meaning of Egyptian hieroglyphs after they had been unreadable for over a thousand years. Jean-François Champollion completed the decipherment in 1822.

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
口 (mouth) — with strokes above depicting a tongue sticking out — the image of speaking, the source of 言's meaning 'speech, words, language.'

example.hanzi: 网上流传的那个传言后来被证实是假的。
example.pinyin: wǎngshàng liúchuán de nàge chuányán hòulái bèi zhèngshí shì jiǎ de.
example.english: The rumor that spread online was later proven to be false.
example.fact: Psychologist Gordon Allport's 1947 research on rumor transmission found that details of a story tend to sharpen and simplify with each retelling, a distortion process called 'leveling and sharpening.' It is the same mechanism that lets a small kernel of truth snowball into a wildly exaggerated rumor.

components.note: 步 (to step, to walk) — suggests repeated motion, one step following another.
页 (a head, turning to look back again and again) — combined with the repeated stepping above, this gave 频 its meaning 'frequent, frequency.'
率 originally depicted a twisted cord or string 幺 being pulled taut in a frame — later extended to meanings like 'to lead' (pulling something along) and 'rate, ratio.'

example.hanzi: 调整收音机的频率才能收听到这个电台。
example.pinyin: tiáozhěng shōuyīnjī de pínlǜ cáinéng shōutīng dào zhège diàntái.
example.english: You have to adjust the radio's frequency to pick up this station.
example.fact: Human ears can typically detect sound frequencies between about 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz, but that range narrows with age — many adults over 50 lose the ability to hear anything above 12,000-15,000 Hz. Elephants, by contrast, communicate using infrasound frequencies as low as 5 Hz, below human hearing, which can travel for kilometers through the ground.

components.note: 手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'
宀 (walls/roof) — the boundary of a home to be protected
寸 (a hand) — keeping watch, holding the space within the walls

example.hanzi: 两名警卫日夜看守着博物馆的大门。
example.pinyin: liǎng míng jǐngwèi rìyè kānshǒu zhe bówùguǎn de dàmén.
example.english: Two guards watch over the museum's entrance day and night.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army, buried over 2,200 years ago to guard Emperor Qin Shi Huang's tomb, consists of more than 8,000 life-sized soldiers, each with individually sculpted facial features — no two faces are exactly alike, suggesting the craftsmen may have used real soldiers as models.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — 资 relates to wealth, funds, and resources.
次 (cì) gives a hint of the sound — 资 is pronounced zī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
力 (strength) — 助 relates to helping, lending one's strength
且 (qiě) gives a loose sound connection to 助's reading zhù

example.hanzi: 这项研究得到了政府的大力资助。
example.pinyin: zhè xiàng yánjiū dédào le zhèngfǔ de dàlì zīzhù.
example.english: This research received substantial funding from the government.
example.fact: The Manhattan Project, the U.S. program that developed the first nuclear weapons during World War II, was subsidized with roughly $2 billion (about $30 billion in today's dollars) and at its peak employed over 130,000 people across sites most of them didn't know were connected.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) reflects an early material used for counting tallies, the origin of 筹's meaning.
寿 (shòu) gives a sound distantly related to chóu, having drifted apart over time.
石 (stone) — 码 originally related to counting stones used for reckoning, extended to mean 'number, code.'
马 (mǎ) is an exact match for the sound of 码.

example.hanzi: 他把手里的筹码全部推到了桌子中间。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ shǒu lǐ de chóumǎ quánbù tuī dào le zhuōzi zhōngjiān.
example.english: He pushed all the chips in his hand to the middle of the table.
example.fact: Casino poker chips are deliberately made heavier than they look — often around 8 to 10 grams each, made from compression-molded clay composites — partly so they feel satisfying to stack and shuffle, and partly to make counterfeiting with cheap plastic harder to disguise.

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 远's meaning 'far, distant,' a long way to walk.
元 (yuán) gives a sound hint — 远 is pronounced yuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 我老远就看见你在路口等我了。
example.pinyin: wǒ lǎoyuǎn jiù kànjiàn nǐ zài lùkǒu děng wǒ le.
example.english: I saw you waiting at the intersection from very far away.
example.fact: The curvature of the Earth limits how far an object can be seen from ground level on a clear day — a person 1.7 meters tall can typically see the horizon only about 4.7 kilometers away, which is why lighthouses and watchtowers were built as tall as possible, to extend the distance ships could be spotted.

meanings: to pass on to sb else

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
辶 (walk/movement) — 递 describes passing something along by moving it from one person to another.
弟 (dì) gives the sound — an exact match with 递.

example.hanzi: 志愿者们把火炬一站一站地传递下去。
example.pinyin: zhìyuànzhě men bǎ huǒjù yī zhàn yī zhàn de chuándì xiàqù.
example.english: The volunteers passed the torch along, one relay station at a time.
example.fact: The modern Olympic torch relay was invented for the 1936 Berlin Games, not ancient Greece — it was devised by German organizing official Carl Diem as a piece of political theater, and the practice of relaying a flame across countries before the opening ceremony has continued at every Games since.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拖 describes pulling or dragging something by hand.
㢟 pictures a foot moving along a long road.
丿 marks a pause or stop in that movement, giving 延 its meaning 'to delay, to extend.'

example.hanzi: 他总是拖延交作业的时间，结果每次都很紧张。
example.pinyin: tā zǒngshì tuōyán jiāo zuòyè de shíjiān, jiéguǒ měicì dōu hěn jǐnzhāng.
example.english: He always delays turning in his homework, so it's always stressful in the end.
example.fact: The word 'procrastination' comes from Latin 'procrastinare,' meaning 'to put off until tomorrow,' and the Roman statesman Cicero used the word as an insult against a political rival — a reminder that complaints about chronic delay are at least two thousand years old.

components.note: 彳 (a path, to walk) — links the character to something worn or displayed while moving about.
幺 (a small strand of silk thread) — 徽 originally named a cord or sash tied on to mark rank, the root of its modern meaning 'emblem, badge.'
音 (sound/music) — represents a musical piece.
十 (ten) — ten musical movements or sections making up a complete piece gave 章 its meaning 'chapter, section, composition.'

example.hanzi: 她把童子军徽章一枚一枚地缝在制服上。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ tóngzǐjūn huīzhāng yī méi yī méi de féng zài zhìfú shàng.
example.english: She sewed the scout badges onto her uniform one by one.
example.fact: The Boy Scouts of America currently offers over 135 different merit badges, ranging from Astronomy to Welding, and a scout must earn 21 specific ones — including mandatory badges like First Aid and Citizenship — to reach the rank of Eagle Scout.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 骗 originally described swinging up onto a horse, later extended figuratively to 'to trick, to swindle.'
扁 (biǎn) shares the rhyme -ian with piàn, and both use a bilabial initial (b/p) — only voicing and tone differ.
尺 (a ruler/measure) — represents rules or measures being set.
口 (mouth) — measures being discussed aloud in one place gave 局 its meaning 'bureau, office, situation.'

example.hanzi: 警方揭露了一起涉及数百万元的投资骗局。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng jiēlù le yī qǐ shèjí shùbǎiwàn yuán de tóuzī piànjú.
example.english: Police exposed an investment scam involving millions of yuan.
example.fact: The Ponzi scheme is named after Charles Ponzi, who in 1920 promised investors 50 percent returns in 45 days by supposedly arbitraging international postal reply coupons; he took in roughly $15 million (well over $200 million today) before the scheme collapsed within about a year.

components.note: An ancient pictograph, possibly of a tool or plow being carried or used — the image of taking up an implement gave 以 its meaning 'to use, by means of.'
彳 (step/walk) — relates directly to 往's meaning 'to go toward, in the direction of.'
王 (wáng) gives a sound hint — 往 is pronounced wǎng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 以往我们从没遇到过这么严重的问题。
example.pinyin: yǐwǎng wǒmen cóng méi yùdào guò zhème yánzhòng de wèntí.
example.english: In the past we never encountered such a serious problem.
example.fact: Ice cores drilled from Antarctica preserve tiny bubbles of ancient air, letting scientists directly measure atmospheric CO2 levels from as far back as 800,000 years in the past — records that show today's carbon dioxide concentration is higher than at any point in that entire span.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 优 originally described an outstanding performer or actor
尤 (yóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 优's reading yōu
止 (a foot, stepping forward) — 先 pictures someone moving ahead of another.
儿 (a person) — one person stepping ahead of another gave 先 its meaning 'before' or 'first.'

example.hanzi: 紧急病人应该优先接受治疗。
example.pinyin: jǐnjí bìngrén yīnggāi yōuxiān jiēshòu zhìliáo.
example.english: Emergency patients should receive treatment with priority.
example.fact: Hospital emergency rooms use a formal system called triage — from the French 'trier,' meaning 'to sort' — first developed on Napoleonic battlefields by French military surgeon Dominique Jean Larrey, who prioritized treating soldiers by the severity of their wounds rather than by rank.

components.note: Two lines curving apart from each other, originally meaning 'to divide, split' — the shape was later adopted to represent the number 'eight.'
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 会议定在明天早上八点开始。
example.pinyin: huìyì dìng zài míngtiān zǎoshang bā diǎn kāishǐ.
example.english: The meeting is set to start at eight o'clock tomorrow morning.
example.fact: Mechanical clocks with hour hands only became common in Europe in the 14th century; before that, most people tracked time using sundials, water clocks, or church bells, and an 'hour' could vary in length depending on the season since daylight was divided into twelve equal parts regardless of how long the day actually was.

components.note: 力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.
囗 (an enclosure) — a garden like 园 is an enclosed area of land.
元 (yuán) gives the sound — an exact match with 园.

example.hanzi: 周末我们打算带孩子去动物园看熊猫。
example.pinyin: zhōumò wǒmen dǎsuàn dài háizi qù dòngwùyuán kàn xióngmāo.
example.english: This weekend we plan to take the kids to the zoo to see the pandas.
example.fact: The Vienna Zoo, founded in 1752 as part of the Habsburg imperial menagerie, is the oldest continuously operating zoo in the world — it began as a private collection of exotic animals for the Austrian royal family before opening to the public decades later.

components.note: 宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'
咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'

example.hanzi: 稳定的收入能给人带来很大的安全感。
example.pinyin: wěndìng de shōurù néng gěi rén dàilái hěn dà de ānquángǎn.
example.english: A stable income can give a person a great sense of security.
example.fact: Psychologist Abraham Maslow placed safety and security needs directly above basic physiological needs like food and water in his 1943 hierarchy of needs, arguing that people cannot fully pursue higher goals like relationships or self-actualization until they feel reasonably secure in their environment.

components.note: 爪 and 彐 (two hands, reaching from opposite sides) — a simplified form of 爭, grabbing for the same thing.
亅 (the object) — what the two hands are struggling over, giving 争 its meaning 'to contend, compete, fight for.'
大 (a person, arms spread wide) — depicts someone in the act of grabbing.
寸 (a hand) — grasping at something, together giving 夺 its meaning 'to seize, take by force.'

example.hanzi: 两个国家为争夺这片油田爆发了冲突。
example.pinyin: liǎng gè guójiā wèi zhēngduó zhè piàn yóutián bàofā le chōngtū.
example.english: The two countries broke into conflict fighting over this oil field.
example.fact: The Spratly Islands in the South China Sea — a scattering of mostly uninhabitable reefs and rocks — are claimed in whole or in part by six different governments, largely because the surrounding waters are believed to sit atop significant untapped oil and natural gas reserves.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 探 describes reaching out with the hand to search for something.
阝 (hill) — 险 originally referred to steep, dangerous terrain
佥 (qiān) gives a sound distantly related to 险's reading xiǎn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 他花了三年时间在亚马逊雨林里探险。
example.pinyin: tā huā le sān nián shíjiān zài Yàmǎxùn yǔlín lǐ tànxiǎn.
example.english: He spent three years exploring the Amazon rainforest.
example.fact: The Amazon rainforest is so vast and dense that scientists estimate previously undocumented species are still being discovered there at a rate of roughly one every two days, including plants, fish, and amphibians never before catalogued.

components.note: 讠 (speech, words) — the middle of the character, an exchange of talk.
辛 (bitter, sharp), placed on both sides, representing the two disputing parties, together giving 辩 its meaning 'to argue, debate.'
扌 (hand) — represents the act of guarding or defending.
户 (door/household) — protecting one's home gave 护 its meaning 'to protect, guard.'
彳 (to walk/step) — represents movement or conduct.
聿 (an old form related to a writing brush) — conduct guided by written rules gave 律 its meaning 'law, regulation.'
帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'

example.hanzi: 被告的辩护律师在法庭上提出了新的证据。
example.pinyin: bèigào de biànhù lǜshī zài fǎtíng shàng tíchū le xīn de zhèngjù.
example.english: The defendant's defense lawyer presented new evidence in court.
example.fact: The right to a defense lawyer even for those who cannot afford one was only firmly established in the United States by the 1963 Supreme Court case Gideon v. Wainwright, after Clarence Earl Gideon, a man too poor to hire an attorney, successfully argued his own appeal from prison with a handwritten petition.

components.note: Hand — digging is done by hand or with a tool held by hand.
Represents a hollow or cave-like shape being dug out.
扌 (hand) — 掘 describes digging with the hands or a tool.
屈 (qū) gives a sound distantly related to 掘's reading jué, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 考古学家在这片沙漠里挖掘出了古代城市的遗迹。
example.pinyin: kǎogǔ xuéjiā zài zhè piàn shāmò lǐ wājué chū le gǔdài chéngshì de yíjì.
example.english: Archaeologists excavated the remains of an ancient city in this desert.
example.fact: The ancient city of Pompeii was buried and preserved almost intact by volcanic ash from Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD, and organized excavation didn't begin until the 1740s — the city sat frozen and hidden for nearly 1,700 years before workers started digging up its remarkably well-preserved streets, buildings, and plaster casts of victims.

components.note: 乂 depicts crossed strokes suggesting a cutting action.
木 (wood) here represents a wooden stake — giving 杀 its meaning 'to kill.'
戈 (dagger-axe) — depicts a dagger-axe, a bladed weapon on a pole, marking the character as related to combat.
翏 (liù) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer closely matches 戮's reading lù.

example.hanzi: 这部纪录片记录了那场战争中的大规模杀戮。
example.pinyin: zhè bù jìlùpiàn jìlù le nà chǎng zhànzhēng zhōng de dàguīmó shālù.
example.english: This documentary records the large-scale massacre that occurred during that war.
example.fact: The passenger pigeon, once North America's most numerous bird with an estimated population in the billions, was driven to extinction within a few decades through unrestricted commercial hunting — the last known wild bird was shot in 1901, and the species went extinct entirely by 1914.

meanings: (to pick) the lesser of two evils

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a peaceful home under a roof relates to 宁's meaning 'calm, serene.'
丁 (dīng) gives a sound distantly related to níng, having drifted apart over time.
丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud

example.hanzi: 他宁可饿着肚子，也不愿意向别人借钱。
example.pinyin: tā nìngkě è zhe dùzi, yě bù yuànyì xiàng biérén jiè qián.
example.english: He would rather go hungry than borrow money from others.
example.fact: During the Great Depression, many unemployed Americans would rather sell apples on street corners for a nickel each than accept government relief, a phenomenon vivid enough that 'apple sellers' became a recognizable symbol of Depression-era pride and desperation in photographs of the time.

components.note: 辶 is the semantic element, tying the character's meaning to walking, movement.
肖 (xiào) shares the same base sound as "xiāo", differing only in tone.
辶 (to walk) shows 遥 relates to distance traveled.
䍃 gives a sound close to yáo, sharing the vowel sound.
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'
夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'

example.hanzi: 这个逃犯已经逍遥法外二十多年了。
example.pinyin: zhège táofàn yǐjīng xiāoyáo fǎwài èrshí duō nián le.
example.english: This fugitive has already been at large, beyond the reach of the law, for over twenty years.
example.fact: D.B. Cooper, who hijacked a Boeing 727 in 1971 and parachuted out with $200,000 in ransom money, remains the only unsolved case of air piracy in American aviation history — despite one of the largest FBI manhunts ever conducted, no confirmed trace of him or most of the money has ever been found.

components.note: 乡 is a simplified form of 鄉, which originally pictured two people facing each other across a shared meal — a scene of communal life that gave rise to the meaning 'village, hometown.'
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 爷爷奶奶一直住在乡下，很少来城里。
example.pinyin: yéye nǎinai yīzhí zhù zài xiāngxia, hěn shǎo lái chénglǐ.
example.english: Grandpa and grandma have always lived in the countryside and rarely come to the city.
example.fact: More than half of the world's population has lived in urban areas only since around 2007, according to United Nations data — for the vast majority of human history, the overwhelming majority of people lived in the countryside, working the land rather than in cities.

components.note: Shell/money — represents wealth or tax paid.
Related to military affairs, since taxes historically funded armies.
An early form showed two hands, one above and one below, passing an object between them — the image of handing something over gave 予 its meaning 'to give, to grant.'

example.hanzi: 法律赋予每个公民平等的权利。
example.pinyin: fǎlǜ fùyǔ měi gè gōngmín píngděng de quánlì.
example.english: The law bestows equal rights on every citizen.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved into a basalt stele around 1754 BC in ancient Babylon, is one of the earliest known written legal codes to formally bestow specific rights and obligations on different classes of citizens, with 282 laws covering everything from trade disputes to family matters.

meanings: variant of 迴避|回避[hui2 bi4]

components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
辶 (to walk) — 避 means to avoid, moving away from something.
辟 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 避.

example.hanzi: 法官因为与被告是亲戚，主动回避了这个案子。
example.pinyin: fǎguān yīnwèi yǔ bèigào shì qīnqi, zhǔdòng huíbì le zhège ànzi.
example.english: The judge voluntarily recused himself from the case because he was related to the defendant.
example.fact: Judicial recusal — a judge stepping aside to avoid even the appearance of bias — has ancient roots; Roman law already held that 'no one should be a judge in his own cause' (nemo judex in causa sua), a principle still cited in courts worldwide today.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — 圈 describes an enclosed loop or pen, as in 'circle, corral.'
卷 (juǎn) shares the rhyme -uan with quān, though the initial has drifted from j- to q- over time.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他在艺术圈子里认识了不少有名的画家。
example.pinyin: tā zài yìshù quānzi lǐ rènshi le bùshǎo yǒumíng de huàjiā.
example.english: He got to know quite a few famous painters within artistic circles.
example.fact: Sociologist Robin Dunbar proposed in the 1990s that humans can maintain only about 150 stable social relationships at once — now known as 'Dunbar's number' — based on a correlation he found between primate brain size and typical social group size across many species.

components.note: 工 depicts a carpenter's square or workman's tool — a simple shape that came to represent work and labor.
禾 (grain) — 程 originally named a unit for measuring grain, extended to 'process, journey, degree.'
呈 (chéng) gives the sound — 程 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.
帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'

example.hanzi: 这座大桥是由一位年轻的工程师设计的。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò dàqiáo shì yóu yī wèi niánqīng de gōngchéngshī shèjì de.
example.english: This bridge was designed by a young engineer.
example.fact: The Brooklyn Bridge's chief engineer, Washington Roebling, was partially paralyzed by decompression sickness after inspecting the underwater caissons during construction, and had to direct the rest of the 1883 project by watching progress through a telescope from his apartment window while his wife, Emily Roebling, managed the site in person.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.
氵 here does not mean water but represents saliva — drooling with desire.
皿 (a vessel/dish) — someone drooling over goods in a dish gave 盗 its meaning 'to steal, thief.'

example.hanzi: 从前这条山路上经常出现强盗打劫过路的商人。
example.pinyin: cóngqián zhè tiáo shānlù shàng jīngcháng chūxiàn qiángdào dǎjié guòlù de shāngrén.
example.english: In the past, bandits often appeared on this mountain road to rob passing merchants.
example.fact: The legendary outlaw Robin Hood, said to have robbed from the rich to give to the poor in medieval Sherwood Forest, may be based on several real outlaws recorded in English court documents from the 13th century, though no single confirmed historical figure matches the legend exactly.

meanings: erhua variant of 一塊|一块[yi1 kuai4]

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
土 (earth/soil) — 块 originally referred to a lump or clod of earth
夬 (guài) gives a sound distantly related to 块's reading kuài, having drifted apart over time
儿 (simplified from 兒) depicts a small child, drawn with a large head on a small body — a simple picture of youth.

example.hanzi: 周末我们一块儿去爬山吧。
example.pinyin: zhōumò wǒmen yīkuàir qù páshān ba.
example.english: Let's go hiking together this weekend.
example.fact: Mountaineers on Mount Everest are required by Nepalese regulation to climb with a certified guide, largely a response to the growing number of solo attempts; even so, more than 300 people have died on the mountain since record-keeping began, many while climbing in groups roped together for safety.

components.note: 戈 (a blade) — 裁 involves cutting.
衣 (clothing) — cutting cloth to make or trim clothing, giving 裁 its meaning 'to cut out, to reduce.'
冫 (a reduced form of 水, water) — 决 relates to water bursting through a barrier, extended to the idea of resolving or settling a matter, hence 'to decide.'
夬 (guài) is close in sound to jué, sharing a similar final though the initial consonant and tone differ.

example.hanzi: 最高法院对这起案件做出了最终裁决。
example.pinyin: zuìgāo fǎyuàn duì zhè qǐ ànjiàn zuò chū le zuìzhōng cáijué.
example.english: The Supreme Court made its final ruling on this case.
example.fact: The U.S. Supreme Court hears oral arguments in only about 60 to 70 cases per year out of roughly 7,000 to 8,000 petitions filed, meaning the overwhelming majority of requests for a ruling are simply denied without any written opinion at all.

components.note: 火 (fire) shows 燃 relates directly to burning.
然 (rán) gives the exact sound of 燃.
米 (rice) — the grain being measured.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring out rice gave 料 its meaning 'material, to estimate, to reckon.'

example.hanzi: 火箭发射需要消耗大量的燃料。
example.pinyin: huǒjiàn fāshè xūyào xiāohào dàliàng de ránliào.
example.english: Launching a rocket requires consuming a huge amount of fuel.
example.fact: The Saturn V rocket that carried Apollo astronauts to the moon burned through roughly 20 tons of fuel and oxidizer per second during liftoff, generating 7.5 million pounds of thrust — most of its total launch weight of 2.8 million kilograms was fuel alone.

components.note: A hand shape reaching down.
A woman, suggesting the idea of being properly managed or settled.
办 (to manage/handle) — 协 relates to people working together to manage something
十 (shí) gives a sound distantly related to 协's reading xié, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 双方经过长时间谈判，最终达成了妥协。
example.pinyin: shuāngfāng jīngguò cháng shíjiān tánpàn, zuìzhōng dáchéng le tuǒxié.
example.english: After lengthy negotiations, both sides finally reached a compromise.
example.fact: The Great Compromise of 1787, struck during the U.S. Constitutional Convention, resolved a deadlock between large and small states by creating a two-chamber Congress — a House of Representatives based on population and a Senate with equal representation per state — a structural compromise that still shapes American government today.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
阝 (a hill/place) — 陆 relates to solid ground, as opposed to water
击 (jī) gives a sound distantly related to 陆's reading lù, having drifted apart considerably over time

example.hanzi: 澳大利亚是世界上最小的大陆。
example.pinyin: Àodàlìyà shì shìjiè shàng zuì xiǎo de dàlù.
example.english: Australia is the smallest continent in the world.
example.fact: Geologists have identified a largely submerged eighth continent called Zealandia, about 94 percent of which lies underwater in the South Pacific — only New Zealand and a few small islands rise above the surface, though the landmass meets all the geological criteria of a continent.

components.note: A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
自 here depicts a head (the character also independently means 'nose, self').
丷 depicts hair atop the head — 首 originally pictured a head with hair, giving its meaning 'head, chief, first.'

example.hanzi: 犯罪嫌疑人最终选择向警方自首。
example.pinyin: fànzuì xiányírén zuìzhōng xuǎnzé xiàng jǐngfāng zìshǒu.
example.english: The criminal suspect ultimately chose to turn himself in to the police.
example.fact: Many legal systems, including China's and several U.S. states, offer reduced sentences for voluntary surrender before arrest, based on the idea that turning oneself in reflects genuine remorse and saves the state the cost and uncertainty of a manhunt.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 草 refers to grass or plants
早 (zǎo) gives a sound close to 草's reading cǎo, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
艹 (grass, plants) — 莓 names low, soft-fruited plants such as berries and moss.
每 (měi) is close to 莓's reading — same base sound, different tone.

example.hanzi: 这个季节的草莓又大又甜。
example.pinyin: zhège jìjié de cǎoméi yòu dà yòu tián.
example.english: The strawberries this season are big and sweet.
example.fact: Botanically speaking, the strawberry isn't a true berry at all — its seeds sit on the outside rather than the inside, and each tiny yellow speck on the surface is actually a separate fruit in its own right, technically making the red flesh an 'accessory fruit.'

components.note: 言 (speech) — 警 relates to speaking out a warning or alarm
敬 (jìng) gives a sound close to 警's reading jǐng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
忄 (heart) — 惕 describes a wary, alert state of mind.
易 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to tì, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 面对陌生人的电话，大家应该保持警惕。
example.pinyin: miànduì mòshēngrén de diànhuà, dàjiā yīnggāi bǎochí jǐngtì.
example.english: Everyone should stay vigilant when receiving calls from strangers.
example.fact: Air traffic controllers are required to take mandatory breaks roughly every two hours because sustained, high-stakes vigilance sharply degrades after that point — a well-documented cognitive effect first studied systematically by psychologist Norman Mackworth during World War II radar operator research.

components.note: 礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

example.hanzi: 希腊神话里有很多关于英雄和怪兽的故事。
example.pinyin: Xīlà shénhuà lǐ yǒu hěn duō guānyú yīngxióng hé guàishòu de gùshì.
example.english: Greek mythology has many stories about heroes and monsters.
example.fact: The myth of the Kraken, a giant sea monster said to attack ships in Norwegian folklore, likely originated from real but rare sightings of giant squid, which can grow to over 12 meters long and were not scientifically confirmed alive in their natural habitat until a specimen was photographed in 2004.

components.note: 令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

example.hanzi: 射箭选手一箭命中了靶心。
example.pinyin: shèjiàn xuǎnshǒu yī jiàn mìngzhòng le bǎxīn.
example.english: The archer hit the bullseye with a single arrow.
example.fact: Competitive Olympic archers shoot at a target 70 meters away with a bullseye just 12.2 centimeters wide — roughly the size of a compact disc — and top athletes routinely hit it, a level of precision made possible partly by compound bows with sighting systems that correct for gravity and wind drift.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 暑 describes the hot weather brought by the summer sun.
者 (zhě) gives a sound distantly related to shǔ, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — represents a human figure.

叚 depicts borrowing or handing something over — a person who is not genuine, or something borrowed rather than real, gave 假 its meaning 'false, fake' (and, for a break from routine, 'vacation, leave.')

example.hanzi: 暑假期间他去外婆家住了一个月。
example.pinyin: shǔjià qījiān tā qù wàipó jiā zhù le yī gè yuè.
example.english: During summer vacation, he went to stay at his grandmother's house for a month.
example.fact: The long summer break in many school calendars is often traced to the 19th-century agrarian school year, when families needed children free to help with the summer harvest — even though most students today have no farm work waiting for them, the extended summer vacation has largely persisted out of tradition.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the one making an offering.
共 (together/both hands) — a person offering something with both hands gave 供 its meaning 'to supply, provide, offer.'
广 (a shelter, overhang) is what remains in the simplified form of the traditional 應, which combined a heart 心 with the phonetic element 雁 (yàn, wild goose).
Although no longer written in the simplified character, the original heart 心 component linked 应 to feeling obliged to respond, the root of its modern senses 'should' and 'to respond.'

example.hanzi: 这家工厂负责向全市医院供应医疗物资。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngchǎng fùzé xiàng quánshì yīyuàn gōngyìng yīliáo wùzī.
example.english: This factory is responsible for supplying medical materials to hospitals across the city.
example.fact: During the Berlin Airlift of 1948-1949, Allied pilots flew over 200,000 flights in under a year to supply West Berlin with food, coal, and other necessities after Soviet forces blockaded all land routes into the city — at its peak, a cargo plane landed roughly every 45 seconds.

components.note: 大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

example.hanzi: 古人常说"天下大事，分久必合"。
example.pinyin: gǔrén cháng shuō "tiānxià dàshì, fēn jiǔ bì hé".
example.english: The ancients often said, "In the great affairs of the world, long division must eventually reunite."
example.fact: The opening line of the classic Chinese novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms — describing the world's cycles of unity and division — has been quoted so often in Chinese political commentary that it is still regularly invoked today when discussing modern geopolitical shifts, some 600 years after the novel was written.

components.note: 米 (rice) — the grain being measured.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring out rice gave 料 its meaning 'material, to estimate, to reckon.'
至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'
刂 (a form of 刀, dāo) gives a sound close to 到's pronunciation dào

example.hanzi: 没人料到这场雨会下得这么大。
example.pinyin: méi rén liàodào zhè chǎng yǔ huì xià de zhème dà.
example.english: No one foresaw that this rain would be so heavy.
example.fact: Modern weather forecasting still cannot reliably predict rainfall amounts for a specific location more than about 7 to 10 days in advance, largely because the atmosphere is a chaotic system — a principle famously illustrated by meteorologist Edward Lorenz's 'butterfly effect,' discovered while running weather simulations in the 1960s.

components.note: 亻 (person) — urging is something one person does to another.
崔 (cuī) gives the sound — an exact match for 催.
目 (eye) — sleep involves closing one's eyes.
民 (mín) gives a sound close to mián, sharing the initial and a similar rhyme.

example.hanzi: 心理医生用催眠的方法帮助他戒烟。
example.pinyin: xīnlǐ yīshēng yòng cuīmián de fāngfǎ bāngzhù tā jiè yān.
example.english: The psychologist used hypnosis to help him quit smoking.
example.fact: Modern clinical hypnosis is recognized by the American Psychological Association as a legitimate therapeutic tool, distinct from the stage hypnosis popularized by entertainers — brain imaging studies have shown that hypnotic suggestion can measurably alter activity in regions of the brain involved in pain perception and attention.

components.note: ⺌ is a remnant of 尚 (a lofty hall) from the traditional form 當, suggesting something set appropriately in a high, visible place.
彐 recalls 田 (a field) from the traditional form — one field matched against another gave 当 its meaning 'to correspond to, to serve as.'
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'

example.hanzi: 包裹当天就送到了，速度真快。
example.pinyin: bāoguǒ dāngtiān jiù sòngdào le, sùdù zhēn kuài.
example.english: The package arrived on that very day — that's really fast.
example.fact: Same-day delivery services trace back further than e-commerce might suggest — department stores in cities like New York and London were offering same-day horse-drawn cart delivery for local purchases as early as the late 19th century, decades before trucks or airplanes existed.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 脚 refers to the foot, a part of the body
却 (què) gives a sound distantly related to 脚's reading jiǎo, having drifted apart over time
足 (foot) — 趾 (the toe) is a part of the foot.
止 (zhǐ) gives the sound — an exact match with 趾's reading.

example.hanzi: 他不小心踢到桌角，脚趾疼了好几天。
example.pinyin: tā bù xiǎoxīn tī dào zhuōjiǎo, jiǎozhǐ téng le hǎojǐ tiān.
example.english: He accidentally kicked the corner of the table, and his toe hurt for several days.
example.fact: Unlike most mammals, humans evolved a relatively short, non-opposable big toe aligned with the other toes, thought to have developed specifically to improve the efficiency of upright walking and running — a trade-off, since it cost our ancestors the ability to grasp branches with their feet the way other apes still can.
